title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This page centralizes Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates. It is intended for all employees, managers, and contractors.

Scope: Applies to all Redwood entities, full-time employees, contractors, vendors with network or data access, and any third party acting on Redwood’s behalf. Operational owners are noted per section.

--

1) Roles & responsibilities (high level)

- People Ops: policy ownership, onboarding/offboarding workflow, travel & expenses governance.
- Security: maintain RBAC standards, review privileged requests, run access audits.
- Finance & Legal: procurement approvals, vendor contracting, expense audits.
- Service owners / Engineering managers: approve access requests for their services and accept operational changes.
- IT / Infra: maintain accounts, SSO integrations, service account lifecycle.

--

2) Access & permissions

Overview: Redwood enforces least-privilege access across all systems. Access is provisioned via the access request workflow and audited quarterly. Multifactor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all accounts.

Key principles:
- Least privilege: grant only the permissions required to perform a role for the shortest reasonable time.
- Role-based access: use groups/roles rather than individual grants where possible.
- Temporary access: time-limited access for escalation or project needs; default expiration of 30 days.
- Just-in-time (JIT) for privileged operations where supported.

Access request flow (standard)
1. Requestor files an Access Request via the Access Request template in Confluence (link in Templates section).
2. Automated SSO workflow routes to the requestor’s manager for approval.
3. Service owner / resource owner approves or denies. If approval, Security is auto-notified for any admin-level request.
4. IT/Infra provisions access and records the change in the Access Audit log.
5. Access auto-expires at the granted end date; re-request required for extension.

Approval matrix (summary):
- Non-sensitive read access: manager approval.
- Write/modify access to production systems: manager + service owner.
- Admin/privileged (root/owner) access: manager + service owner + security approver (two approvers required).
- Access to customer PII or Restricted datasets: manager + security + data-owner signoff.

Service accounts and secrets
- Service accounts must be registered in the Service Account Registry and scoped to the minimal permissions.
- Secrets must be stored in the company-approved secret manager (KMS/HSM integration).
- Secrets rotation: 90 days for high-risk secrets; 180 days for other service secrets.

Onboarding / offboarding
- New hires: People Ops triggers account creation (SSO) and default role assignments based on role templates.
- Offboarding: People Ops initiates immediate deactivation in SSO, revokes all cloud console access, and creates a post-offboarding audit task for managers to confirm access removal.
- Contractors: All contractor accounts are time-limited and require sponsor confirmation every 30 days.

Audit & review
- Quarterly access review: Managers must review and attest to active members of their teams. Security runs automated orphaned-account reports monthly.

--

3) Change management

Purpose: Ensure changes to production services, core infrastructure, and sensitive configurations are reviewed, scheduled, and auditable.

Change categories
- Standard changes: pre-approved, low-risk operational tasks (e.g., routine backups, patching windows documented in runbooks).
- Normal changes: require RFC (Request for Change), peer review, and CAB approval if impacting production.
- Emergency changes: immediate action required to mitigate outages or security incidents; must be followed by a post-facto RFC within 48 hours.

RFC process for normal changes (step-by-step)
1. Author creates an RFC using the Change Request template (link in Templates). Include impact analysis, rollback plan, test plan, and owners.
2. Peer review by the owning engineering team.
3. Security and SRE review for changes affecting auth, networking, or persistent data.
4. Schedule through the Change Calendar; if production-impacting, present to the weekly CAB (Change Advisory Board) with at least 72 hours notice.
5. CAB decision recorded (approve/reject/defer).
6. Implement per the schedule; operations team completes implementation checklist and records outcome.
7. Post-change review within 5 business days for any substantial change.

Emergency change process:
1. Implement emergency mitigation immediately.
2. Notify incident channel and on-call, and create a post-facto RFC within 48 hours.
3. CAB performs expedited review in the next 24-72 hours after stabilization.

Rollback and testing
- Every change must include an explicit rollback plan and a validated test plan for the affected components.
- Staged rollouts (canary/A-B) are encouraged for behavior changes.

Change windows and blackout periods
- Weekly maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00-06:00 UTC for non-critical updates.
- Blackout periods: deploy freezes around major launches, quarterly earnings, or other company-declared events; declared by Product and Operations.

--

4) Data management

Data classification
- Public: information cleared for external release.
- Internal: non-sensitive business data (default).
- Restricted: internal data with potential business impact if disclosed (e.g., roadmaps, internal analytics).
- Confidential / Highly Restricted: customer PII, health or regulated data, or data covered by contract.

Handling rules by classification
- Public: no special controls; review before publishing.
- Internal: stored on company systems; standard access controls.
- Restricted: access via role-based grants; encryption at rest & in transit required.
- Confidential: additional contract/legal controls, encryption (KMS/HSM), access approval by data owner, and mandatory logging.

Retention & deletion
- Financial records: retain 7 years (Finance).
- Employment records: retain 7 years after separation (People Ops).
- Product telemetry: default 1 year; aggregate metrics may be retained longer at anonymized resolution.
- Customer personal data: retention governed by contract and data subject requests; default archival at 2 years unless otherwise specified.

Backups & recovery
- Backups are automated, encrypted, and verified weekly. Restore drills are performed quarterly for critical services. Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) targets are documented in service-level runbooks.

Encryption & key management
- All sensitive data must be encrypted at rest and in transit. Keys are managed via the company KMS; production keys have documented rotation policies.

Data access requests and data removal
- Data access for analytics or support requires a Data Access Request with justification and expiration.
- Data deletion for customer requests follows the Data Subject Request (DSR) flow owned by Legal + Privacy.

--

5) Procurement & expenses

Overview: Centralized procurement is managed by Finance; People Ops owns travel & employee expense policies. All purchases must follow the approval matrix.

Approval thresholds (examples)
- <= $5,000: Manager approval.
- > $5,000 and <= $50,000: Manager + Finance approval.
- > $50,000: Manager + Finance + Legal (and VP or higher for strategic contracts).

Procurement process (steps)
1. Raise a Purchase Requisition (PR) using the Procurement template; include business justification, budget code, and preferred vendor.
2. Finance reviews PR for budget and compliance.
3. For approved PRs, generate Purchase Order (PO) and send to vendor.
4. Vendor issues invoice; Finance matches invoice to PO and issues payment per net terms.

Card & expense policy
- Corporate cardholders must complete cardholder training.
- Employees submit expenses via the Expense submission system within 30 days of spend; receipts required for all transactions.
- Reimbursable categories: travel, training, approved software subscriptions, client entertainment (requires manager pre-approval).
- Non-reimbursable: personal expenses, family travel, alcohol without business purpose.

Exceptions and emergency purchases
- Emergency purchases outside normal approval thresholds require post-facto approval and a documented justification. Repeat emergency spending by the same team will trigger procurement review.

--

6) Vendor management & onboarding

Risk tiers and required artifacts
- Low risk: commodity services (e.g., office supplies). Minimal onboarding; standard PO.
- Medium risk: SaaS tools with business data (e.g., analytics platforms). Require Data Processing Agreement (DPA), basic security questionnaire, and finance terms.
- High risk: vendors handling customer data, PII, or providing critical infrastructure (e.g., hosting, identity). Require SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, penetration test results, DPA, contract SLAs, and legal review.

Vendor onboarding checklist
1. Business sponsor creates Vendor Onboarding form (template).
2. Security runs vendor security assessment and requests evidence (SOC reports, penetration test summary).
3. Legal reviews and approves contract terms (DPA, IP, indemnity, SLA).
4. Finance assigns payment terms and PO as required.
5. Vendor is added to the Vendor Registry with assigned risk classification and renewal date.

Vendor performance & renewal
- Annual review for medium/high risk vendors focusing on security posture, SLAs, and cost-effectiveness.
- Contract renewals triggered 90 days before contract end; Business sponsor and Finance must confirm continuing need.

--

7) Travel policy and expense guidance

Booking & approvals
- All travel must be pre-approved using the Travel Request template.
- Employees should use preferred vendors and partner booking tools where available to ensure compliance with travel insurance and preferred rates.

Allowances & class of travel
- Domestic flights: economy allowed; upgrades require manager + People Ops approval.
- International flights > 8 hours: premium economy may be allowed with manager approval; business class requires VP approval.
- Per diem: $75/day domestic; $200/day international (adjust for high-cost cities via travel portal).
- Lodging: reasonable nightly rate based on city guidelines; employees should select best-value options that meet safety standards.

Expense submission
- Submit expenses within 30 days using the Expense system with itemized receipts. Card charges should be reconciled weekly by cardholders.
- Lost receipts: submit Lost Receipt Form with manager approval; reimbursement subject to Finance discretion.

Safety & travel insurance
- The company provides business travel insurance for approved trips. Emergency contact and local security guidance must be consulted for high-risk regions.

--

8) Internal templates and attachments

Canonical templates (links)
- Access Request template: /templates/access-request-template
- Change Request (RFC) template: /templates/change-request-template
- Vendor Onboarding template: /templates/vendor-onboarding-template
- Procurement / Purchase Requisition template: /templates/procurement-pr-template
- Travel Request template: /templates/travel-request-template
- Expense Report template: /templates/expense-report-template
- Service Account Registration: /templates/service-account-registration

Each template includes required fields, example entries, approver list, and expected SLAs for review. Use the templates to ensure approver routing and auditing metadata are captured in the source-of-truth systems (ServiceNow / Workday / Procurement tool).

--

9) Monitoring, compliance, and enforcement

- Periodic audits: Security + Finance run joint audits (quarterly) to ensure access controls, procurement compliance, and vendor contract adherence.
- Non-compliance: policy violations are handled according to HR discipline guidelines and may include revocation of access, financial restitution, or termination.
- Policy updates: People Ops coordinates policy changes; updates are communicated via All-Hands and via the Confluence changelog.

--

10) Frequently asked questions (short)

Q: Who do I contact for an access exception?
A: Submit an Access Exception Request and include manager approval; Security will evaluate. Exceptions are time-limited (max 30 days) and require documented business justification.

Q: How do I onboard a new vendor quickly?
A: Use the Vendor Onboarding template, provide the requested security artifacts, and tag the request as ‘urgent’ in the procurement system. Expect expedited review for high-priority business needs but the same minimum artifacts apply.

Q: Who approves a software subscription under $2,000/year?
A: Manager approval is sufficient for subscriptions under $5,000/year; Finance should be informed for budgeting.

--

11) Appendix: approval matrix (text table)

| Request type                          | Approver(s) required                         | Notes |
|---------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|-------|
| Non-sensitive read access             | Manager                                      | Auto-expire 30d |
| Production write access               | Manager + Service owner                      | Require RFC for changes |
| Admin/privileged access               | Manager + Service owner + Security           | Two approvers + audit log |
| Purchases <= $5k                      | Manager                                      | PO optional |
| Purchases $5k–$50k                    | Manager + Finance                             | PO required |
| Purchases > $50k                      | Manager + Finance + Legal (+ VP for >$250k)  | Contract review required |
